newsitem.title: ROMANIA: OUTGOING ROMANIAN MINISTER DEFENDS GOVERNMENT.
newsitem.headline: OUTGOING ROMANIAN MINISTER DEFENDS GOVERNMENT.

text.p: Romania's outgoing finance minister on Wednesday said the leftist government, defeated in elections, had left the economy in better shape than at the beginning of its four-year term.

Florin Georgescu said the government had achieved growth of 18.1 percent during its term, reduced unemployment to seven percent from 10 percent and reduced arrears of state companies to 21 percent of gross domestic product from 70 percent. It had also returned Romanians' purchasing power to 1992 levels.

"Things are better now than in 1992 when we took over," Georgescu told a news conference. "We have achieved good fiscal and budgetary discipline, more efficient public expenditure and lower inflation, while fostering solid economic growth."

The government of Prime Minister Nicolae Vacaroiu, in office since October 1992, pursued what it called cautious reforms intended to cushion the population at large from austerity associated with the transition to the market.
It is to be replaced next week by a centrist coalition which accuses it of widening the gap in living standards with ex-communist states like Poland and Hungary.
Georgescu acknowledged on Tuesday that the government had revised figures upward for inflation and the budget deficit.

Inflation was now likely to hit 38 percent by the end of the year against earlier forecasts of 30 percent and the budget deficit 4.0 percent of GDP instead of 3.0 percent. Both figures far exceed recommendations by the International Monetary Fund.
The Fund suspended credit payments to Romania this year.
"The factors which led to Romania not being able to stick to its commitments to the IMF were primarily economic and only in a small proportion political," Georgescu told reporters.
He blamed poor agricultural output and a decision to meet demands for wage rises in an election year.
Romanian economists say the chances of restoring IMF credits are much improved since the reformists' election win.
